name: Land an ollie
blurb: The trick every other skate trick is built on: the board leaves the ground with you, unattached. It is a timing puzzle, and it takes far longer than beginners expect.
gear: Somewhere flat, and grass or carpet for the first attempts
steps: Learn it stationary first, with the board wedged in grass or carpet so it cannot shoot out.
Set your feet: back foot on the tail with the ball of your foot on the very end, front foot behind the front bolts.
Snap the tail down hard and jump at the same moment — the pop and the jump are one action, not two.
Drag the outside of your front foot up the grip tape towards the nose. This is what levels the board out.
Suck your knees up and level the board in the air, then land over the bolts with bent knees.
Once it works stationary, do it rolling slowly. Rolling ollies are easier than stationary ones, oddly.
tips: No pop usually means your back foot is not on the very tip of the tail.
The board flying forwards means you are not dragging your front foot, just jumping.
This one takes weeks. Everyone who lands it went through the same frustrating fortnight.
proof: You ollie over a stationary obstacle while rolling, and land rolling away.
